subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'sanctity of life' mean?
options: The belief that human life is holy and sacred because it is given by God
The belief that all living things are equally valuable
The idea that life should always be free from suffering
The view that only religious people have valuable lives
questions.explain: Sanctity of life is the Christian belief that life is holy and God-given, so it must be respected and protected.

questions.q: The teaching that humans are 'made in the image of God' comes from which book of the Bible?
options: Genesis
Exodus
Matthew
Romans
questions.explain: Genesis 1:27 states that God created humankind in his own image, underpinning the sanctity of life.

questions.q: The word 'euthanasia' comes from Greek words meaning what?
options: Good death
Final release
Painless sleep
Merciful end
questions.explain: 'Euthanasia' derives from the Greek for 'good death', often described as ending life to relieve suffering.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines abortion?
options: The deliberate termination of a pregnancy
The natural loss of a pregnancy
A method of preventing conception
The premature birth of a healthy baby
questions.explain: Abortion is the deliberate ending of a pregnancy before the baby can survive independently.

questions.q: Situation ethics as an approach to moral decision-making was developed by which person?
options: Joseph Fletcher
Thomas Aquinas
John Calvin
William Barclay
questions.explain: Joseph Fletcher developed situation ethics in the 1960s, teaching that the loving thing to do is the right thing.

questions.q: In Christian ethics, what does the term 'agape' refer to?
options: Selfless, unconditional love
Romantic love between partners
Loyalty to one's family
Friendship between believers
questions.explain: Agape is selfless, unconditional love and is the central guiding principle in situation ethics.

questions.q: Which statement expresses the 'Golden Rule' taught by Jesus?
options: Do to others as you would have them do to you
Love God with all your heart
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth
Turn the other cheek to those who wrong you
questions.explain: The Golden Rule (Matthew 7:12) tells believers to treat others as they would wish to be treated.

questions.q: In Roman Catholic teaching, marriage is regarded as which of the following?
options: A sacrament
A civil contract
An optional tradition
A private agreement
questions.explain: The Catholic Church teaches that marriage is a sacrament, a sacred and lifelong bond blessed by God.

questions.q: Why does the Roman Catholic Church teach that marriage is indissoluble?
options: Because it is a lifelong bond joined by God that only death should end
Because divorce is illegal in most countries
Because couples must stay together for financial reasons
Because the Bible never mentions marriage ending
questions.explain: Catholics teach that what God has joined together should not be separated, making marriage lifelong.

questions.q: Why do many Roman Catholics object to the use of artificial contraception?
options: They believe sexual intercourse should remain open to the possibility of new life
They believe all family planning is forbidden
They believe couples should never have children
They believe contraception is too expensive
questions.explain: Catholic teaching holds that sex within marriage should stay open to procreation, so artificial contraception is opposed.

questions.q: How does the belief in the sanctity of life shape many Christians' view of euthanasia?
options: They oppose it because only God has the right to end a human life
They support it because suffering should always be avoided
They are neutral because the Bible commands euthanasia
They support it only for elderly people
questions.explain: Because life is seen as God-given and sacred, many Christians believe humans should not choose to end it.

questions.q: A Christian who strongly holds the sanctity of life would most likely regard abortion as...
options: Wrong, because life is God-given and should be protected from conception
Acceptable in all circumstances
A purely medical matter with no moral weight
Required whenever a pregnancy is unplanned
questions.explain: The sanctity of life leads many Christians to view abortion as wrong because it ends a God-given life.

questions.q: According to situation ethics, how should a Christian decide the right course of action?
options: Do whatever is the most loving thing in that particular situation
Always follow fixed rules without exception
Do whatever brings the greatest personal benefit
Only act when the Church gives permission
questions.explain: Situation ethics judges each case by agape love, doing whatever is most loving rather than following fixed rules.

questions.q: What role does conscience play for many Christians when making ethical decisions?
options: It acts as an inner, God-given guide to what is right and wrong
It replaces the need for any religious teaching
It always agrees with the government's laws
It only matters for religious leaders
questions.explain: Many Christians see conscience as an inner voice, given by God, that helps guide moral choices.

questions.q: Which best describes a difference between Roman Catholic and many Protestant views on divorce?
options: Catholics generally do not permit remarriage in church after divorce, while many Protestants may allow it
Protestants forbid all divorce while Catholics encourage it
Both Churches treat divorce in exactly the same way
Neither Church allows marriage at all
questions.explain: Catholic teaching sees marriage as indissoluble, whereas many Protestant Churches accept divorce and remarriage in some cases.

questions.q: Why do many Christians turn to the Bible when facing an ethical decision?
options: They regard it as authoritative and the word of God
They believe it contains scientific laws
They think it is the only book worth reading
They use it only for historical facts
questions.explain: Many Christians treat the Bible as an authoritative source of moral guidance because they believe it reveals God's will.

questions.q: A nurse who follows situation ethics must decide whether to break a hospital rule in order to comfort a dying patient. Situation ethics would tell her to...
options: Do whatever is the most loving thing in that situation
Always obey the rule no matter what
Refuse because rules can never be broken
Ask another patient to decide for her
questions.explain: Situation ethics puts agape love first, so the most loving action is the right one even if a rule is broken.

questions.q: A man with a terminal illness asks a Christian friend to support his request for euthanasia. Basing her response on the sanctity of life, she would most likely...
options: Encourage him to accept care and palliative support, as only God should end life
Immediately agree because his suffering must be ended
Agree because he alone owns his life
Ignore him because the issue is too difficult
questions.explain: Holding the sanctity of life, she would oppose euthanasia and instead support compassionate care.

questions.q: A Catholic couple whose marriage has broken down completely wish to remarry other people in church. According to Catholic teaching, they...
options: Cannot remarry in church unless an annulment is granted
Can freely divorce and remarry whenever they wish
Must remarry within one year
Can remarry only in a registry office
questions.explain: Because Catholics see marriage as indissoluble, church remarriage is only possible if the first marriage is annulled.

questions.q: Applying the Golden Rule, how should a Christian treat a stranger who is in need of help?
options: Treat the stranger as they themselves would wish to be treated
Help only if the stranger belongs to their own religion
Ignore the stranger unless asked twice
Help only if it brings a reward
questions.explain: The Golden Rule instructs believers to treat others as they would want to be treated, showing care to those in need.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Religious Studies (2017) specification; An Introduction to Christian Ethics
